# `passportsim net_http`

Report the virtual LAN, or bridge an allowlisted port to a server on the host.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Caps group | `radio` |
| MCP tool | `passport_net_http` |
| HTTP route | `POST /v1/instances/{id}/commands/net_http` |
| Scenario step | `net.http` |
| CLI aliases | none |
| Annotations | `needs_instance` |

## Hosts

The matrix below is the full one; this page is byte-identical on every host.

| macOS | Windows | Browser |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | yes |

## Synopsis

```text
passportsim net_http [--host-port <HOST_PORT>] [--instance <INSTANCE>] [--op <OP>] [--port <PORT>] [--json <@file|->]
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Form | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `host_port` | `--host-port <HOST_PORT>` | `integer` | no | bridge: the 127.0.0.1 port it reaches (default: port). |
| `instance` | `--instance <INSTANCE>` | `string` | no | Instance id. |
| `op` | `--op <OP>` | `"status"` \| `"bridge"` \| `"unbridge"` | no | Default status. |
| `port` | `--port <PORT>` | `integer` | no | bridge: the guest port on host.emu.internal. |
| `routes` | carried by `--json` | `array` | no | - |

A nested object or array is passed as one JSON document with `--json @<file>` or `--json -`; it has no flag of its own.

Input schema: [`docs/schema/commands/net_http.input.json`](../schema/commands/net_http.input.json).

## Examples

### Show the LAN, its HTTP service and the bridge

```sh
passportsim net_http --json - <<'JSON'
{}
JSON
```

```powershell
@'
{}
'@ | passportsim net_http --json -
```

### Bridge the guest's port 80 on host.emu.internal to a host server on 8080

```sh
passportsim net_http --json - <<'JSON'
{
  "host_port": 8080,
  "op": "bridge",
  "port": 80
}
JSON
```

```powershell
@'
{
  "host_port": 8080,
  "op": "bridge",
  "port": 80
}
'@ | passportsim net_http --json -
```

### Detach the bridge

```sh
passportsim net_http --json - <<'JSON'
{
  "op": "unbridge"
}
JSON
```

```powershell
@'
{
  "op": "unbridge"
}
'@ | passportsim net_http --json -
```
